#3170. RMR Group (RMR) Q4 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Fiscal fourth quarter results beat guidance as a multiyear REIT overhaul advances.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

The RMR Group Inc. (RMR +6.62%) reported fiscal fourth quarter results that exceeded internal guidance, supported by operational improvements and strategic asset sales across its managed REIT platform. Management stated that the company is executing a multiyear plan to transition SVC into a pure play triple net lease REIT, involving the sale of 77 retained hotels by the end of calendar 2028. The firm reported that it has significantly reduced office exposure within its managed mortgage REIT and is prioritizing deleveraging across its equity REIT clients to navigate a higher-for-longer interest rate environment. Despite a global slowdown in commercial real estate fundraising, the company is focusing on brand awareness and technological investments, including artificial intelligence, to drive operating leverage and long-term private capital growth.

Operator: Good day, everyone, and welcome to the RMR Group Fiscal Fourth Quarter 26 Results Investor Conference Call. All participants will be in a listen only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To withdraw your questions, you may press star and 2. Please note today's event is being recorded. At this time, I would like to turn the floor over to Bryan Anthony Maher, senior vice president. Please go ahead.

Bryan Anthony Maher: Good morning, and thank you for joining RMR's fiscal fourth quarter 26 conference call. With me on today's call are President and CEO, Adam David Portnoy Chief Operating Officer, Matthew Paul Jordan and Chief Financial Officer, Matthew C. Brown. In just a moment, they will provide details about our business and quarterly results, followed by a question and answer session. I would also like to note that the recording and retransmission of today's conference call is prohibited without the prior written consent of the company. Today's conference call contains forward looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 2 thousand and other securities laws.

These forward looking statements are based on RMR's beliefs and expectations as of today, November 13, 2026, and actual results may differ materially from those that we project. Company undertakes no obligation to revise or publicly release the results of any revision to the forward looking statements made in today's call. Additional information concerning factors that could cause those differences contained in our filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission which can be found on our website at rmrgroup.com. Investors are cautioned not to place undue reliance upon any forward looking statements. Addition, we may discuss non GAAP numbers during this call. Including distributable earnings and adjusted EBITDA. A reconciliation of net income determined in accordance with U. S.

Generally Accepted principles to these non GAAP figures can be found in our financial results. With that, I will now turn the call over to Adam.

Adam David Portnoy: Thank you, Bryan, and good morning, everyone. The fourth quarter capped off a productive fiscal year for our platform. As both continued operational improvements and the ongoing execution of strategic actions were seen across our clients. While we also continued our efforts to expand our private capital business. Our quarterly results were highlighted by distributable earnings of $17.2 million or $0.53 per share, and adjusted EBITDA of $21.5 million with both measures exceeding the high end of our guidance. Our REIT management teams have worked to improve operating performance, strengthen balance sheets, optimize capital allocation and improve portfolio quality.

Many of these initiatives remain in the early stages and have the potential to support additional earnings growth and shareholder value creation in the years ahead. I would now like to speak about some selected highlights across our managed REITs. At DHC, strong operating results were highlighted by same property SHOP occupancy increasing 200 basis points year over year to 84.4% while same property SHOP NOI increased more than 50% year over year to $48 million DHC also recently announced that it had entered into a new 15-year triple net lease with the Ensign Group for a portfolio of skilled nursing facilities which is expected to improve cash flows while reducing DHC's future CapEx.

Further, DHC announced that the remaining 76 shop communities not already operating under revised management agreements will transition to updated structures effective January 1, 2027. These transitions are expected to further align operator incentives with property level performance to increase cash flows and shop communities in the future. 7 Hills, our commercial mortgage REIT continued to productively deploy capital funding more than $120 million in new loans this quarter which represented the highest level of quarterly origination activity in 5 years. Additionally, 7 Hills has successfully reduced its office exposure to approximately 10% with limited losses realized as part of that effort.

7 Hills remains committed to its dividend and expects to achieve sustainable dividend coverage during the first half of calendar 27. Given the meaningful reduction in office exposure, the strong demand for its flexible financing solutions and the attractive opportunity set in middle market commercial real estate, we believe 7 Hills is well situated to drive earnings growth, which will also benefit RMR given our significant ownership stake in the company. At SBC, the significant investments that the REIT has made over the past few years are starting to show up in its results. In the third quarter, SVC's 77 retained hotels grew RevPAR 8.3% outperforming The US hotel industry for the eighth consecutive quarter.

And the adjusted hotel EBITDA grew 16.2% year over year. Alongside announcing its results last week, SVC also outlined operating initiatives that it believes could add approximately $109 million of EBITDA to its 77 retained hotels over the next 12 to 24 months. In addition, SVC illustrated that with this increased cash flow, the 77 retained hotels could be worth between $3 billion and $4.1 billion in aggregate. As a reminder, SVC is in the middle of executing a multiyear plan to transition from being principally a hotel REIT into a pure play triple net lease REIT.

At the same time, SVC is focused on reducing leverage from its current above market leverage ratio of 9x net debt to adjusted e. EBITDA to no more than 5x which would be in line with its triple net lease REIT peers. As part of this plan, SVC has sold 142 mostly select service hotels for $1.1 billion and largely used the proceeds to repay debt over the last 3 years. With this as background, I wanna take a few moments to address the publicly disclosed letters that SVC has received over the last several weeks. In early October, a company called TKO issued a public letter which offered to buy SBC's hotel for $2 billion.

They followed up by issuing a press release in mid October with. Which largely reiterated their desire to buy the hotels. it is worth noting, however, that TKO has never reached out directly to s SBC or RMR asking to engage in any discussions nor have we had any prior business relationship with them And the only communications we have seen from TKO are the same ones that the public has seen. Last week, the SBC board, all 6 of its independent trustees, unanimously rejected the TKO offer. The principal reason was that the offer was significantly below what management and the SBC Board believe SBC's retained hotel portfolio is worth.

And especially what it believes these hotels will be worth after EBITDA significantly increases over the next 12 to 24 months. Shortly after announcing earnings last week, SVC received another publicly disclosed letter from an investment firm called Blackwells. Similar to TKO, Blackwells made no direct outreach to SVC or RMR before issuing its public letter. The letter from Blackwell's makes numerous claims and demands but in essence, it wants SVC to immediately sell all its remaining hotels at the highest price available today. As this call began, SVC issued a press release that includes a letter from SVC's board responding to Blackwells.

After talking with many SVC shareholders over the last several weeks, I think it is important for me to make clear some things about SVC's plans to sell its remaining hotels and to remove any ambiguity or confusion in the marketplace about RMR's motivations and incentives with regards to managing SVC. As the manager of SVC, RMR is 100% committed to transitioning it into a pure play triple net lease REIT. At the same time, we think it is important that SBC emerges from this transition at significantly lower leverage so that the company can be successful going forward.

To that end, it is not a matter of if SVC will sell its remaining hotels, but a matter of when is the right time to do so. With that in mind, I would like to expand on when we currently think is the right time. To sell the 77 re. Retained hotels at SVC. First of all, we have already largely pruned the hotel port portfolio. Having sold nearly all the underperforming hotels. And what is left is a portfolio of 77 performing hotels that are well positioned for significant cash flow growth.

Given that SVC has spent $628 million renovating these hotels over the last 3 years, and that we believe EBITDA is likely to increase by roughly $109 million over the next 12 to 24 months It is our view that SBC should allow EBITDA to grow at the hotels over the coming months before selling them. In order to maximize their values. Said simply, we believe will receive significantly higher proceeds in the future as hotel EBITDA improves rather than be a forced seller of these hotels today. In what we believe would be lower values I would also like to discuss how we see future hotel sales at SBC unfolding.

Because the 77 retained hotels are a mixed collection of select service, upscale, and upper upscale hotels located in suburban, airport, urban, and resort locations, it is our view that it will likely receive significantly higher total proceeds selling these hotels individually or in small portfolios rather than in 1 large transaction. Also, given that the timing of EBITDA improvement will vary by hotel, It is our view that these sales will likely happen through multiple transactions starting in 2027 with the goal of selling substantially all of the hotels by year-end 2028.

With regard to how SBC will sell these hotels, we think they will likely be sold through competitive marketed processes using experienced brokers similar to how we sold the prior 142 hotels over the last 3 years. Nevertheless, if SBC were to receive an unsolicited offer from a credible party that values an individual hotel small portfolio, or the entire portfolio of hotels ahead of our timeline at a price that is close to what we believe they would be worth in the future after the cash flow increases significantly then we would, of course, seriously consider it together with SVC's board as a means to accelerate SVC's transition to a delevered pure play triple net lease REIT.

Finally, I want to address RMR's motivations and incentives in managing SVC. RMR's contract with SVC is highly aligned with SVC shareholders. RMR's management fee is currently calculated based on SVC's total market capitalization. So if SVC stock goes up, RMR makes more money. And if SVC stock goes down, RMR makes less money. RMR also has the opportunity to earn meaningful incentive fees tied to SVC's total shareholder return compared to its peers. Finally, RMR recently made a $50 million investment in SVC. Which further aligns RMR with SVC shareholders and makes RMR 1 of SVC's largest shareholders.

While earning higher management fees as SVC stock price improves is obviously attractive, The opportunity to earn meaningful incentive fees along with a high return on investment in SVC is very compelling for RMR. Said plainly, RMR is highly incentivized to manage SBC in a manner that would benefit all SVC shareholders. With that, I will now turn the call over to Matthew Paul Jordan.

Matthew Paul Jordan: Thanks, Adam. While a number of our clients have benefited from improvements in operating fundamentals, the broader macroeconomic environment remains challenging. Higher interest rates, inflation, and geopolitical uncertainty have weighed on commercial real estate fundraising with global fundraising this past quarter reaching its lowest level since 2012. Despite these headwinds, we continue to believe the long term opportunity in private capital remains compelling and continues to represent a significant pool of monies dedicated to real estate investing. While recent fundraising efforts for RMR sponsored vehicles have been muted, we remain focused on increasing RMR's brand awareness, and strengthening relationships with institutional investors to position us to capitalize as fundraising conditions improve.

To that end, as a diversified real estate manager, we are finding increasing levels of interest from institutional investors as they seek out managers whose vertically integrated platform can generate alpha through operational innovation. As investors learn about investments we have made in technology, consumer marketing, centralized operational cost containment, and most importantly, our deep bench of investments and operations professionals, we are finding new investor engagement heading into calendar 2027 across a number of the sectors RMR manages. As it relates to RMR's operating margins, as our clients have executed on their ongoing strategic investments, most notably asset sales, we have remained focused on ensuring that RMR's platform reflects those changes.

In response to these asset sales, we have been diligent in rightsizing portions of the organization where operating and asset management requirements require less resources. These actions together with continued expense discipline contributed to a 460 basis point sequential increase in adjusted EBITDA margin, to 45.9% during the fourth quarter. While we have rationalized resources in certain functional areas, we have continued to make strategic investments to support our long term growth. For example, over the past year, we have expanded our marketing and capital formation efforts and increased investments in technology. We are also actively deploying artificial intelligence across our platform to ensure RMR remains at the forefront of AI innovation.

Beyond obvious back office productivity gains, our primary focus has been establishing tools that assist in investing and underwriting, as well as driving NOI improvements at our managed assets. These investments have allowed us to drive significant operating leverage. As demonstrated by AUM per employee increasing from $77 million in 2021 to over $105 million today which we expect will only continue to expand. Taken together, we believe the combination of a more efficient operating platform, targeted investments in growth initiatives, and continued value creation leaves RMR well positioned With that, I will turn the call over to Matthew C. Brown.

Matthew C. Brown: Thanks, Matthew, and good morning, everyone. For our fiscal fourth quarter, we reported adjusted EBITDA of $21.5 million and distributable earnings of $0.53 per share both of which exceeded our guidance. Recurring service revenues were $45.2 million, a modest sequential quarter decrease, was in line with our expectations largely driven by nearly $600 thousand of acquisition fees earned last quarter. These decreases were partially offset by higher construction supervision fees and total market capitalization improvements at DHC and ILPT. Next quarter, we expect recurring service revenues to decline to approximately $43.9 million, largely driven by recent total market capitalization declines at certain of our managed equity REITs. Turning to expenses.

Recurring cash compensation was $38.9 million, a sequential quarter decrease of approximately $700 thousand driven by headcount rationalization and the cumulative compensation adjustments we recognized in the prior quarter. Our cash compensation reimbursement rate increased to approximately 45% this quarter. Looking ahead to next quarter, we expect recurring cash compensation to be approximately $38 million with a reimbursement rate of approximately 43%. As noted on last quarter's call, RMR's annual share awards to employees occurred in September which increased our non reimbursable, non cash equity based compensation by approximately $700 thousand this quarter. Recurring G&A this quarter was $9.7 million, a sequential quarter decrease of approximately $1 million driven primarily by reductions in normal course legal fees.

We expect recurring G&A to increase slightly next quarter. Below the operating line, we recognized a $22.7 million loss on investments this quarter largely reflecting non cash unrealized losses from changes in the share prices of certain of our investments during the quarter. These unrealized losses were the primary driver of our GAAP net loss of $12.4 million and are excluded from adjusted EBITDA and distributable earnings. As noted on prior calls, quarterly tax rate is subject to fluctuation. This quarter, we recognized an income tax benefit of approximately $2 million primarily reflecting the unrealized losses on our investments and our effective tax rate for the full fiscal year was 17.8%, consistent with the range we previously guided to.

For modeling purposes, we expect our tax rate to be approximately 16% for fiscal 27. Aggregating these collective assumptions, next quarter we expect adjusted EBITDA to be approximately $18.5 million to $19.5 million, a sequential quarter decline largely driven by the declines in total market capitalization at certain of our managed REITs. #3169. Epic formally asks SCOTUS to uphold contempt ruling against Apple

Epic Games has submitted its official response to Apple’s Supreme Court appeal, urging the justices to uphold the contempt ruling over App Store payment restrictions. Here are the details.

As most 9to5Mac readers probably know, Apple and Epic Games have been engaged in a lengthy legal battle since 2020, when Epic sued Apple after Fortnite was removed from the App Store.

The move came after Epic remotely activated an alternative payment system that bypassed Apple’s In-App Purchase system.

Although the court largely sided with Apple, it did rule that the company could no longer prevent developers from directing users to alternative payment methods outside the App Store.

Apple ultimately allowed those links, but imposed new restrictions, including a 27% commission on external purchases, in addition to new rules limiting how developers could display buttons and links to alternative payment methods.

Epic challenged those restrictions, and the court agreed that Apple had violated the original injunction, holding the company in civil contempt.

Apple has since attempted multiple times to overturn that ruling, arguing that the original injunction contained no explicit prohibition on imposing those restrictions.

Epic, on the other hand, argues that Apple deliberately circumvented the court order by introducing new rules designed to achieve the same result as those originally prohibited.

In May, Apple appealed to the Supreme Court, which agreed in June to hear the case. Apple submitted its opening brief in September, followed by supporting briefs from the U.S. government and several legal and business groups.

Those included the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Chamber of Progress, and several former federal antitrust enforcers. In a nutshell, the U.S. government argued that the original injunction did not clearly prohibit Apple’s 27% commission on external purchases, but maintained that the company was correctly held in contempt for restricting how developers could display external payment buttons.

In its opening brief, Apple argues, citing multiple legal precedents, that courts must enforce the letter of an injunction rather than its broader spirit.

According to the company, there was nothing in the original injunction explicitly prohibiting it from charging commissions on external purchases or imposing additional restrictions on payment links, so it should not be held in contempt for conduct that the court order did not clearly prohibit.

In its response filed today, Epic disputes Apple’s interpretation of the injunction, arguing that the company “attempts to avoid contempt by proposing an extreme legal standard.”

[Apple] argues that a court can find contempt only if an injunction spells out the exact practice at issue–so an injunction barring Apple’s then-existing anti-steering rules left it free to implement new ones that prevent steering just as effectively. Nothing in this Court’s precedents supports that approach, which would reduce injunctions to a never-ending game of whack-a-mole.

Epic argues that “Apple devised a plan to circumvent the injunction,” claiming that “Apple chose a rate of 27% for the commission, knowing that, when combined with the developers’ payment-handling costs (more than 3%), the rate for linked-out purchases would be higher than the rate for purchases using Apple’s payment system.”

As an Apple executive admitted, every “linked-out transaction is going to be more expensive to any developer * * * than an IAP transaction at 30 percent.” Apple simultaneously commissioned a “sham” report to try to provide an economic justification for the commission; the report contained an “entirely manufactured” rationale for the 27% rate.

The company also argues that “Apple tried to cover up its scheme to circumvent the injunction” by asserting privilege over more than 57,000 documents, and points to Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers’ finding that “its Vice President of Finance ‘outright lied under oath’ when he testified about when Apple decided to impose the new commission.”

Finally, Epic asks the Supreme Court to uphold the contempt ruling against Apple or, if the justices decide to clarify the legal standard for contempt, to send the case back to the lower courts for reconsideration under that standard.

With Epic’s response now filed, Apple has until December 14 to submit its final brief before oral arguments take place on January 11, 2027.

#3164. Biofrontera (BFRI) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Liquidity concerns and a new skin cancer indication shape the quarter.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Biofrontera Inc. (BFRI -24.39%) reported third-quarter results highlighted by the FDA approval of Ameluz for the treatment of superficial basal cell carcinoma and a favorable ruling from U.S. Customs and Border Protection regarding its redesigned RhodoLED XLC lamp. Management stated that the new indication makes Ameluz the first photodynamic therapy approved in the United States for a skin cancer. The company filed a supplemental New Drug Application to expand the use of Ameluz to the extremities, neck, and trunk, with a regulatory decision date assigned for Aug. 2027. Operations during the quarter were impacted by legal and remediation costs associated with the International Trade Commission matter, though the company reported a reduction in the sales volume affected by the exclusion order. Management detailed a mitigation plan to address liquidity concerns, including focusing on revenue growth from the new indication and potentially drawing on a working line of credit.

Operator: Welcome to the Biofrontera, Inc. Third Quarter 26 Financial Results and Business Update Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in listen-only mode. After today's prepared remarks, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Please note this event is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Ben Shamsian with Lytham Partners Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Ben Shamsian: Good morning, and welcome to Biofrontera's Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Business Update Conference Call. Please note that certain information discussed during today's call by management is covered under the Safe Harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act. We caution listeners that Biofrontera's management will be making forward-looking statements that actual results may differ materially from those stated or implied by these forward-looking statements due to risks and uncertainties associated with the company's business.

Forward-looking statements on today's call include statements regarding the timing and success of the commercial launch of Ameluz for superficial basal cell carcinoma the company's supplemental new drug application for actinic keratosis, on the extremities, neck, and trunk, effects of the International Trade Commission orders, the company's remediation plan and the RhodoLED XLC the outcome of pending appeals and patents proceedings, the company's liquidity, its ability to continue as a going concern and its plans to address that condition and the company's compliance with NASDAQ continued listing standards. All risks and uncertainties are detailed in and are qualified by the cautionary statements contained in the Biofrontera's press releases and SEC filings.

Including the company's quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, which the company expects to file later today and the company's annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025. Also, conference call contains time sensitive information that is accurate only as of the date of this live broadcast. Biofrontera undertakes no obligation to revise or update any forward-looking statements to reflect events or circumstances after the date of this conference call except as required by law.

During today's call, there will be references to certain non GAAP financial measures, Biofrontera believes these measures provide information for investors yet should not be considered as a substitute for GAAP nor should they be viewed as a substitute for operating results determined in accordance with GAAP. A reconciliation of non GAAP to GAAP results is included in the press release issued today and is available on the company's website at www.biofronteraus.com. Under the Investor Relations section. Please note management will be referencing adjusted EBITDA and non GAAP financial measure defined as net loss excluding interest expense, net income taxes, depreciation and amortization, and certain other non recurring or non cash items.

Including changes in fair value of warrant liabilities, and of the related party investment patent remediation expense, and ITC related inventory write downs and stock based compensation. With that said, I would now like to turn the call over to Hermann Luebbert, CEO, Chairman, and Founder of Biofrontera. Hermann.

Operator: Please proceed. Sir, is your line on mute perhaps?

Hermann Luebbert: Yes. I was on mute. Thank you, Ben, and thanks everyone for joining us this morning. Do you hear me now?

Hermann Luebbert: Great. So the third quarter changed what the company is able to sell and to whom. With 2 things happening within 5 days of each other, in September, and I want to start with both of them before we get to the numbers. On September 9, the FDA approved Ameluz photodynamic therapy for the treatment of superficial basal cell carcinoma in adults. That makes Ameluz the first PDT approved in The United States to treat a skin cancer. Until now, our label has been limited to mild to moderate actinic keratosis on the face and scalp. We now have a second indication.

Superficial basal cell carcinoma represents up to 20% of all basal cell carcinomas, the most common cancers in The United States. Many of these patients are today treated surgically. Ameluz PDT gives dermatologists a nonsurgical option with a favorable cosmetic outcome that they can deliver to the RET with the red light lamp that is already in the office. Furthermore, we believe that the approval to treat a skin cancer will convince more doctors to introduce Ameluz PDT as a routine treatment in the offices and purchase 1 of our red light lamps.

Then on September 14, 5 days after the SB. sBCC approval, US Customs and Border Protection ruled that our redesigned large field lamp which we called RhodoLED XLC, does not infringe the asserted claims of the DUSA Pharmaceutical patents and is not subject to the exclusion order in issued by the International Trade Commission or ITC earlier in the year. Let me put that into context. The ITC orders took effect on July 6. From that date, we could not import or sell the original RhodoLED XL, and we could not sell Ameluz for use with it. Customers with only, whose only lamp was the RhodoLED XL were temporarily unable to buy Ameluz from us.

But in light of the September 14 CBP ruling, we can now sell the RhodoLED XLC, providing our prior RhodoLED XL customers with a large 5 panel lamp that is unrelated to the ITC orders to go alongside our smaller BF-RhodoLED lamp, which is similarly not affected by the ITC orders. And of course, we can continue selling Ameluz to any customers who have either an XLC or a BF-RhodoLED lamp. By September, the number of customers ordering from us was back to the level of a year ago. I said on our last call that we will not allow our commercial plan to depend on winning in court and that is how it turned out.

We designed around the patents obtained the favorable ruling, had no objections from the FDA, and are working through the remediation of the affected lamps in the field which we expect to be substantially complete by the end of the second quarter of 27. We will furthermore file our appeals with the Federal Circuit both of the commission's determination and of the patent office director's decision. I will not speculate on the timing or outcome of those appeals. This matter did cost us in the quarter.

Fred will take you through the detail about legal fees, remediation costs, and inventory write downs tied to the ITC matter are the main reason our operating loss was larger than in the second quarter. I regard most of this as the cost of getting to the other side of the problem. Now to the pipeline. Because it is the clearest picture of how this company grows in 2027 and beyond. First, superficial basal cell carcinoma. We expect to begin commercializing Ameluz for SBCC with a full launch in the first quarter of 2027 after receiving FDA feedback on our anticipating anticipated marketing material. The launch goes into our existing installed base of lamps and our existing dermatology call points.

George will describe the preparation. Second, actinic keratosis on the extremities, neck, and trunk. Early In early October, we submitted our supplemental new drug application to expand the Ameluz label beyond the face and scalp to treat AK on the entire body. FDA has confirmed a PDUFA date of August 5, 2027 and initiated its preliminary review. AK is in most cases a UV light induced disease, and occurs on all body parts frequently exposed to the sun. Such body parts can be larger than face and scalp. And we applied for a treatment field of up to 240 square centimeters, centimeters supported by the positive phase 3 results we announced earlier this year.

As PDT on larger areas is often associated with more pain, we furthermore filed with FDA an illumination protocol that is expected to reduce this pain. With approximately 58 million American adults, having at least 1 AK lesion, treating the extremities, neck, and meaningfully expands the use of Ameluz in every 1 of our customers' offices and on every lamp already in the field. So the picture is this. 1 year ago, we had 1 indication and a transfer price that took 25% to 35% of our revenue away. Today, we own the U.S. assets. We have 2 approved indications, a third filed and a LAMP portfolio that is clear of the ITC exclusion order.

Each of the indications runs for the same lamps and the same sales force. I would now like to turn the call over to George Jones, our Chief Commercial Officer. George?

George Jones: Thank you, Hermann, and good morning, everybody. Product revenues in the third quarter were $9.1 million an increase of approximately 30% year-over-year. Ameluz unit volume grew approximately 23% with the balance of the growth coming from a price increase we implemented in the fourth quarter of 2025 as well as increased lamp sales that occurred during the quarter. In the third quarter, we sold approximately 25,100 tubes of Amluz up 23% from 20,400 in Q3 of 2025. I would like to drill a little deeper into the results. In June into early July, ahead of the ITC orders taking effect, a number of customers purchase Ameluz earlier than they otherwise would have.

Because of those purchases, we had a fast start to the quarter. We ensured customers received ample supply of Ameluz to treat their patients while we worked on the remediation efforts Hermann spoke about earlier. This higher July was simply a shift in timing and we believe that this inventory was largely worked through by the end of Q3. It is important to remember that the ITC orders only impacted approximately 200 customers and 25% of our Ameluz sales volume. And the rest of our customers could continue to purchase Ameluz as normal. Moving on to lamps. We ended the quarter with an installed base of 853 lamps across 742 different dermatology offices.

This includes approximately 12 of the small RhodoLED lamps that were sold during Q3 to customers that wanted a Biofrontera light red light, but did not want to wait until the XLC was available. This is good news. We began processing exchanges of the XLC lamps upon receiving customs and border protection approval. They began shipping during Q3, but were not installed until early October. As I think back on the quarter, I am especially pleased by the progress we made on the remediation efforts Hermann mentioned.

By placing both RhodoLED and XLC lamps in offices that previously purchased the XL lamps, we have been able to significantly reduce the percentage of sales impacted by the 25% of Ameluz volume to only 10% of Ameluz volume sales volume today. Turning to sales execution, I could not be more impressed with this Biofrontera team They have never met a challenge that they have not been able to overcome. We are seeing significant momentum in our business. All key sales metrics were positive year-over-year, both in Q3 as well as the first 9 months of the year.

In Q3, orders were up 6% year-over-year, tubes per order were up 21% and new locations buying Ameluz increased by 11% or 39% year-over-year. Looking at 2026 year-to-date, tubes of Ameluz were up 23%, number of orders were up 13% and tubes per order were up 10% year-over-year. Furthermore, in 2026, we have seen lower turnover within our sales force as well as a positive impact of our new inside sales efforts, which is contributing to our overall results. Moving on to SBCC and launch preparation.

I would like to start by saying there is been significant early interest in learning more about Ameluz for superficial basal cell carcinoma and a clear belief from our customers that this new indication provides meaningful differentiation between Ameluz red light PDT and our competitors. As we mentioned earlier, we are launching using a phased approach for which Phase 1 is underway. I would like to call out some Phase 1 highlights for you. We have begun talking to KOLs about the sBCC data and received great feedback. We have confirmed our reimbursement strategy. As Hermann mentioned, we have submitted our marketing claims to the FDA for their feedback.

Our full product training is beginning this week and our launch meeting is scheduled for mid January. Importantly, to support the launch, I want to reiterate that we will be using our current sales infrastructure and calling on many of the same dermatology offices who are already equipped and ready to expand their utilization and offer their patients an innovative nonsurgical option to treat their basal cell carcinoma. We are looking forward to the fourth quarter and finishing 2026 strong. With that, I will turn the call over to Fred Leffler, our Chief Financial Officer. Fred.

Eugene Frederick Leffler: Thank you, George, and good morning, everyone. Walk through our results for the third quarter and first 9 months ended September 30, 2026. All comparisons are to the same prior year period unless otherwise noted. Full reconciliation of GAAP to non GAAP measures is included in our press release that we filed earlier this morning and is available on our website. Okay, revenues for the third quarter were $9.1 million, compared to $7.0 million last year, an increase of 29.8%. As George described, unit volume grew 23.3%, or 3.3%, or approximately $1.6 million. With the balance from the fourth quarter 2025 price increase and higher device sales.

Substantially, all of that volume growth reflects approximately $1.6 million of orders placed in early July, ahead of the ITC effective date The increase reflects Ameluz unit volume growth or sorry. For the first 9 months, revenues were $31.2 million, up 26.6% from $24.6 million. The increase reflects Ameluz unit volume growth of approximately $5.5 million including about $3.6 million from accelerated order timing and approximately $700,000 from the fourth quarter 2025 price increase. Cost of revenues for the quarter were $2.3 million compared with $2.0 million producing a gross profit of $6.7 million and gross margin of 74.4% compared to 70.7% in 2020 the year before in 2025. An improvement of approximately 370 basis points.

The improvement comes from the cost structure we put in place with the strategic transaction that Hermann mentioned earlier, which is Ameluz direct clot cost plus a 12% earn out on net revenue. The third quarter margin is lower than the roughly 80% we reported in the first half a couple of reasons. First, lamp and device costs were $400,000 higher, driven by higher lamp sales and $300,000 of RhodoLED lamp inventory write downs including a $200,000 write down of XL long-term raw materials and work in process. For the 9 months, gross margin was 78.0%, compared to 67.7% in the prior year.

Selling, general and administrative expenses including the related party line, was $12.5 million for the quarter compared to $10.4 million the year before, an increase of $2.1 million The main drivers were $1.1 million increase in general and administrative expense, mostly $900,000 of higher legal fees related to the ITC matter. $700,000 of cost in manufacturing and in regulatory and product affairs which are functions we took over, with the strategic transaction last year. And $500,000 of higher direct sales expense, namely commissions on higher Ameluz volumes were partly offset by $300,000 of decreases in related-party SG&A.

For the 9 months, SG and A was $33.2 million compared to $29.6 million an increase of $3.5 million Research and development expenses were $500,000 for the quarter compared to $900,000 and $1.8 million for the 9 months compared to $2.9 million reflecting the substantial completion of our clinical trials. Patent remediation expense was $300,000 in the quarter and $700,000 for the 9 months. Let me give you the full cost of the ITC matter to date outside of the legal fees since it sits in more than 1 line. Through September 30, we have recognized total charges of $1.1 million made up of $600,000 of accrued remediation costs And $500,000 of inventory write downs.

Of the remediation costs, $200,000 was settled with inventory used in the remediation program and $0.4 million is paid or payable in cash. Net loss for the quarter was $6.4 million or $0.42 per share compared with a net loss of $6.6 million, or $6.02 per share last year. For the 9 months, net loss was $11.8 million or $0.89 per share compared with $16.2 million in 2025, or $1.67 per share. Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was negative $5.5 million compared with negative $6.0 million and adjusted EBITDA margin of negative 60.9% against a negative margin of 80.7% last year.

For the 9 months, adjusted EBITDA was negative $9.3 million compared to negative $15.5 million a margin of negative 29.7% against negative 63.0%. The third quarter is seasonally our weakest and this year it also absorbed some weak ITC legal spend which was not backed into adjusted EBITDA. Turning to the balance sheet and liquidity, as of September 30, 2026, we had cash and cash equivalents of $3.2 million compared with $6.4 million at December 31, 2025. Cash used in operating activities for the 9 months of 2026 was $3.2 million, down from $11.0 million a year ago. Total liabilities were $21.7 million compared to $81.1 million at year-end 2025.

Our only outstanding indebtedness is about $4.7 million of convertible notes net maturing in November 2027, have no bank or long term debt. As a result of Q3, stockholders' deficit was $200,000 at September 30, 2026, So we do not currently meet minimum stockholders' equity requirements of NASDAQ. But we expect to file our form 10 k and intend to submit a plan to regain compliance as needed. I want to address the going concern disclosure directly as well.

As described in our Form 10-Q, which we will file, which we will file later today, management has concluded that, substantial doubt exists about the company's ability to continue as a going concern for at least 12 months From the issuance of our form 10 q. Our plan to mitigate has 4 parts. They will be laid out in the queue. Continuing to grow analyst revenue, with Q4 typically our strongest quarter. Including supported by the sBCC launch while controlling expenses. Obtaining and drawing on a working line of credit, the next $1 million milestone payment from our [Inaudible] divestiture which we expect in December and which depends on the purchaser achieving certain milestones.

And if necessary, raising additional capital through equity or debt. Some of these are not within our control, and these plans have not alleviated the substantial doubts. With that overview of our financial results, we are now ready to take questions from our covering analysts. Operator?

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session from our covering analysts. To ask a question, you may press star then 1 on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, please press star then 2. And as a final reminder, if you would like to ask a question, please press star then 1 at this time. And our first question today comes from Bruce Jackson at StoneX. Please go ahead.

Bruce Jackson: Hi, good morning and thanks for taking my questions. I just wanted to look at the operating expense profile going into the fourth quarter. So third quarter had several special charges. Where do you see that core rate for cost of goods sold? And so what catch of gross margins are we going to be looking at? And then with the SG and A, maybe you could give us kind of a rough indicator of where that might shake out?

Eugene Frederick Leffler: Hi, Bruce. Yeah. Thanks for asking. So on the gross profit, I expect that to be back around our 80% mark. Nothing to my knowledge, for the first quarter should push that down like the charges did in Q3. With regarding to SG and A, generally, we have been doing. Aside from the legal points that I mentioned, we have been doing an excellent job of managing our costs. Doing what we need to do to support the business, So I expect that to you know, continue, and we will manage the legal costs you know, as needed.

Bruce Jackson: Okay. And then, you mentioned that you are putting together the reimbursement strategy for the superficial basal cell carcinoma indication. Do you have is reimbursement going to be available when you launch that? And do you have a rough idea of what that might be?

George Jones: Yeah. I will take that. We believe that there will be a clear path to reimbursement upon launch of the indication We are in the market right now working with some key customers I will say, kind of confirming that strategy. And relative to exactly how much it is going to be for the customers, the tubes of Ameluz will be reimbursed as normal. Via the J code and then the procedure codes we are finalizing kind of what we think that is gonna be for the customer.

Bruce Jackson: Okay. Got it. Thank you very much.

Operator: Thank you. That concludes our question and answer session. I would like to turn the call back over to management for any closing remarks.

Hermann Luebbert: Yes. Thank you, operator, and thank you to everyone who joined us today. Let me leave you with 3 takeaways. First, Ameluz is now the only PDT drug in The US approved for skin cancer. Superficial basal cell carcinoma is our second US indication and we begin commercializing it later this quarter and into the first quarter of 27. Second, the ITC matter is no longer limiting which customers we can serve. The XLC is cleared. Our customers are ordering again. And the remediation is on a defined path. Third, the third quarter shows the cost of getting here. And we are not hiding from it.

Our cash position requires discipline, and I have told you how we plan to address it. What has changed is what we have to sell. 2 indications today and a third filed all delivered through the lamps and the sales force already in place. I want to thank our entire team for their dedication and hard work. I also want to thank our shareholders health care professionals who use our products, and most importantly, the patients whose lives we are helping to improve within the fight against skin cancers. Thank you for your continued support Have a wonderful day.

Operator: Thank you. The conference has now concluded. Thank you for attending today's presentation. You may now disconnect and have a wonderful day.

#3163. Top Wall Street analysts are upbeat about the prospects for these 3 stocks

September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Neocloud company CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

Recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

Chatterjee said CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

"CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," said Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

Chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

After a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

Over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and new markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security company, Powell said. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

Meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell said.

BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

Powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

In a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he said.

Devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

Additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

Overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the company if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he said. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

"Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," said Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

Devitt ranks No. 765 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 49% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

#3162. How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain – and what you can do

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

New research provides a stark look at the AI supply chain and the risks it brings to businesses.

Artificial intelligence companies worldwide are bringing a new wave of vulnerabilities and security issues to the digital supply chain, researchers warn.

According to a new report published by Black Kite on Tuesday, there now exists a “widespread cybersecurity weakness” across the “rapidly expanding ecosystem of companies developing, deploying, and supporting artificial intelligence.”

AI and smart solutions don’t automatically equate with safe solutions. In a study titled “2026 AI Supply Chain Report: The Risks Behind Your AI Relationships,” Black Kite says that many AI suppliers — the companies that develop and deploy AI services to today’s businesses — are struggling with “basic security practices.”

Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?

According to the research, after examining the companies themselves, along with their software, integrations, and components, researchers found failures to patch critical vulnerabilities, protect credentials, authenticate users and email, and address network security issues.

The study analyzes 18,160 AI companies worldwide, ranging from 0-10 employees to more than 1,000 employees. A company’s AI involvement was determined through reviews of company products and services and primary business activities, covering six broad groups: everyday application development; AI development and implementation; AI applications in specialized sectors such as healthcare, IT, and finance; industrial organizations; and AI foundations working on data, compute, and modeling.

A small percentage of assessed companies are considered “unclassified,” and the study excluded businesses that use AI only incidentally.

In addition, unusual network activity was detected at 44.3% of organizations, and botnet-related activity was recorded at 41.8% of AI companies.

AI’s main business appeal is its ability to integrate with existing software and platforms to handle manual tasks, heavy lifting, and tedious, time-consuming work, freeing employees to focus on work that requires human oversight.

Enterprises are investing billions of dollars in AI. Menlo’s 2026 research estimates that enterprise AI spend reached $37 billion in 2025, with half of overall spend going to AI apps. In total, 76% of enterprise AI solutions are purchased rather than built internally.

However, the moment an AI or automated component is introduced into a corporate ecosystem or operational platform, any security problems it has impact the user — and each additional integration, such as software components or open-source tooling, may also increase the attack surface.

In an accompanying analysis of AI firms’ use of Model Context Protocol (MCP) components, which can link AI apps to business systems, 48.8% of 1,732 logged security findings were rated High or Critical, including code and command injection vulnerabilities.

Also: The new enterprise AI expert every company needs

It’s not just the AI application itself. As noted by Black Kite, AI suppliers often have access to customer data, developer environments, business infrastructure, and enterprise platforms. If the supplier’s credentials are stolen, this could expose its customers to a range of cyberattacks.

The researchers found, for example, that 19.9% of AI companies offering solutions for enterprise AI deployment had corporate login information in infostealer records, and that stolen corporate logins, overall, were linked to 6.8% of AI suppliers in the study.

Visibility matters, too, for businesses that should be monitoring their digital supply chains. However, 33.2% of AI companies assessed have a “limited” digital footprint, including their domains, subdomains, and IP addresses.

The same principles for protecting the digital supply chain apply to AI suppliers, where continual monitoring and assessment are among the best protections businesses have.

Staying informed and aware of the risks to your own business makes all the difference. As recommended by Black Kite, it takes more than a single point-in-time security assessment — frequent monitoring and engaging with suppliers to understand their technologies and dependencies can reveal potential security issues.

Also: Do you need AI agent liability insurance?

If you find weaknesses, manage them by priority, handling ransomware-related exposures and vulnerabilities actively exploited in the wild first.

Also audit an AI tool’s integrations and components, access, what data it can reach, and the potential impact of exploitation. Once you’re armed with this information, it’s possible to weigh risk and reward — and whether the AI tool is worth the potential attack exposure it brings. If you decide to keep it, limit its permissions and access to what it requires.

#3160. Ring’s new drone patrols your home to keep an eye on things – even upstairs

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Home & Office > Smart Home > Home Security

Alongside the Ring Drone Cam, Ring introduced the Rover Cam for businesses. It investigates disturbances and streams 4K footage.

Today, Ring announced the launch of a new subbrand, Ring Robotics, with two new products: the $249 Ring Drone Cam, an indoor “mobile security camera” drone that shoots 2K video, and the $999 Ring Rover Cam, a security robot for businesses that patrols autonomously and investigates disturbances.

Also: Amazon’s new Echo Studio gives Alexa+ an AI camera to see inside your home

Both devices use Ring’s custom navigation software, “AI Pilot,” to autonomously navigate interior spaces and move between set points along a patrol, rather than being controlled directly by the user. AI Pilot leverages the devices’ cameras, sensors, and vision models, along with cloud processing, to create interior maps, then move the devices between predesignated patrol points such as a side door or a window.

I recently saw both new robots in person at a showcase in New York hosted by Ring’s founder and chief inventor, Jamie Siminoff. They certainly do what they advertise but come with some significant limitations. The drone, for example, can only stay in the air for about 8 minutes before it needs to dock and recharge, while the Ring Rover Cam is slow and deliberate, seemingly ideal for routine surveillance rather than rapid response to an event.

The Ring Drone Cam moves around predetermined patrol points in your home, sending you a live 2K video feed whether you’re just in another room or out of town. The user doesn’t actually fly the drone; instead, it moves around autonomously using Ring’s custom “AI Pilot” navigation technology, leveraging its cameras, sensors, and cloud processing to create a map of its surroundings. This allows it to fly through the air at an appropriate height, going from room to room, even up stairs.

In the Ring app, the user creates patrol points they want the drone to move between — likely a window, doorway, or high-traffic room — creating a set path that is both predictable (so you always know where the drone will go) and relevant, so it’s only monitoring the areas you want it to. But here is where its limitations come into play: It needs a finite path to navigate because its flight time is limited to just five to eight minutes in the air before it has to return to its charging dock.

That makes the dock both the start and end point for the drone’s routine trips, and it’s designed with this in mind. When it goes to land, the drone hovers over the dock and lowers itself down, dropping into place so it can start charging automatically. I asked about its potential to land elsewhere, and Ring told me it would only make an emergency landing outside of its dock in case it didn’t have enough power to get home.

Also: Amazon’s new Echo Dot can turn into a Wi-Fi extender – how it works

There’s one other very important caveat: This thing is loud. There’s no sneaking up on anyone with the Ring Drone Cam, as the entire household is likely to hear it the second it undocks. The four propellers emit a constant, high-pitched whirring while in the air that’s loud enough to announce its presence to anyone in the vicinity: intruder or resident.

During the product briefing, Siminoff insinuated that this was part of its design to dissuade home intruders snooping around your house at night (especially when paired with the drone’s front-facing spotlight), but it’s likely just the result of its engineering, especially considering this is a first-gen product. It’s so loud that it makes me think it’s better suited to navigating the home when no one’s home (although whether or not your pets go bonkers trying to catch it is a whole other issue).

The Ring Drone is designed to work out of the box with the existing Ring ecosystem, including the 2K Video Doorbell and Indoor Cam, and is also compatible with Amazon’s Map View.

The Ring Drone Cam will start shipping on Jan. 27, 2027, and will cost $249.

The other product Ring announced is the Rover Cam, a mobile robot with a 4K camera designed to monitor large spaces like warehouses, offices, or businesses. Ring calls it a “security guard that never clocks out,” but it’s more like a slow-moving droid that goes on set patrol paths. It leverages the same AI Pilot technology as the Ring Drone to map its surroundings and navigate around shelving, furniture, and obstacles in real time.

It’s much quieter than its airborne sibling, traveling at low speeds and offering mobile surveillance instead of wiring every square inch of a large space. If the technology here looks familiar, it’s because it resembles the Amazon Astra, a smaller robot designed for home monitoring but with a very similar build.

The idea here is to deploy the robot to certain areas of a workplace via the app, then get 360-degree views once it’s there. Like the drone, it can also set out on automated routes at select timing intervals — like right after a business closes or before it opens. During working hours, it chugs along with its camera, capturing everything in its view.

Also: The 4 biggest Amazon smart home announcements from today

If another Ring device is triggered, the Rover Cam autonomously goes to investigate the disturbance, providing 4K footage in real time via the app. It also features a periscope camera that can extend to see over obstacles like shelving, counters, or furniture, providing a high-level view if needed. In case you lose it in a large warehouse or office, it has a “light tower” that projects light upward onto the ceiling, notifying users of its location.

Even when docked, it uses motion-sensing technology to start recording the second it senses any kind of movement, just like Ring doorbell cameras. In case of an emergency, the Rover features a siren and red flashing lights to dissuade intruders.

The Ring Rover Cam is available for preorder now and will start shipping on Dec. 16, 2026. It will cost $999.

#3159. Moving iMage (MITQ) Q1 2027 Earnings Call Transcript

Accelerated projects helped the quarter beat prior outlook despite margin pressure.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Moving iMage Technologies, Inc. (MITQ +12.94%) reported financial results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, highlighting growth in total revenue and the attainment of net profitability. Management attributed the quarterly performance to the acceleration of specific customer projects and the ongoing integration of the Digital Cinema Solutions loudspeaker product line. The company indicated that its expanded product portfolio, including premium large-format and immersive audio technologies, addresses current capital investment priorities from theater exhibitors. Management stated that the business continues to evaluate strategic combinations to enhance its market position and financial results.

Operator: Greetings, and Welcome to the Moving iMage Technologies first quarter 2027 earnings call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. A question-and-answer session will follow the formal presentation. If anyone should require operator assistance, please press star ,on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. It is now my pleasure to introduce Chris Eddy with Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Chris Eddy: Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining today's call. MiT President Francois Godfrey will provide a business overview, and CFO Bart Bedard will discuss some financial highlights, after which we will open the call to investor questions. Today's conference is being recorded, and an audio replay and written transcript will be posted to the investors section of the Moving iMage website in the next few days. As a reminder, except for historical information, the matters discussed on this call are forward-looking statements that involve several risks and uncertainties.

Words like believe, expect, and anticipate mean that these are our best estimates as of this writing, but that there can be no assurances that expected or anticipated results or events will take place. Actual future results could differ materially from those statements. Further information on the company's risk factors is contained in the company's quarterly and annual reports filed with the SEC. I will now turn the call over to MiT President Francois Godfrey.

Francois Godfrey: Thanks, Chris, and thank you all for your interest in Moving iMage Technologies. We are pleased with our first quarter performance, as it benefited from some of the positive underlying dynamics within the exhibition industry, including two customer projects which were accelerated into the period. As a result, our first quarter revenue rose by 9.2% to $6.1 million, benefiting from DCS loudspeaker sales and increased customer project activity in preparation for the critical holiday feature film release window. The accelerated project timelines caused our Q1 performance to exceed our earlier outlook.

Of course, the timing of small and large projects can easily shift a few quarters as customers move implementations forward or back to meet internal operating or financial goals or priorities, creating potential variability in our quarter-over-quarter results. Importantly, we were able to generate positive net income for the quarter. While we don't want to overemphasize the significance of a single reporting period, I do want to highlight the skill and dedication of our team to serving customers while maintaining a disciplined approach to operating efficiency. As we pursue new avenues of growth potential, we remain firmly focused on building a sustainable business model with the potential to generate profitable growth.

As I alluded, we remain encouraged by the industry backdrop and solid box office performances, which are traditionally the strongest indicators for capital investments in new or upgraded cinema technology. Movie industry analysts continue to express optimism about the film slate over the next 12 months, supported by renewed customer enthusiasm for the theatrical experience. We believe this provides exhibitors with greater confidence in the long-term prospects of their business while also providing needed cash flow to fund new equipment and auditorium upgrades. We believe our expanded product portfolio, including PLF and immersive audio solutions, positions us well to participate in these opportunities as exhibitors evaluate their capital investment priorities for the coming year.

As exhibitors seek to maximize attendance, premium large-format auditoriums and immersive audio solutions remain a key pathway to differentiate their venues and enhance the moviegoing experience. Given the technical complexity and scope of such projects, they remain important revenue opportunities for MiT. I am pleased to report that we are seeing a more robust level of activity in our industry, and we are engaged in discussions surrounding several potential projects that could contribute to our business in calendar 2027. These conversations include some meaningful potential opportunities for LEA Professional amplifiers, an industry-leading product line we began working with four years ago and is continuing to gain long-term operational acceptance.

The addition of the DCS loudspeaker line to our business has helped build interest by enabling us to offer a comprehensive audio solution. Having referenced DCS, let me provide an update on the acquisition, which we closed early in the second quarter of last fiscal year. Overall, we are very pleased with how things are going, though there have been some challenges in incorporating the DCS operations into MiT and ramping up our manufacturing and global logistics. As we expected, customer interest is very strong, both with legacy DCS customers around the world and with new prospects.

However, it does take time to rebuild the rapport with each customer and to build trust and credibility about our commitment to the quality and service they expect. Our team is progressing well in this regard in a financially disciplined manner. The net result is that we continue to see great value in expanding our base of proprietary products to provide us entry and competitive advantage in the marketplace. It takes time to establish ourselves with this product, but since closing the acquisition about a year ago, our team has generated total sales of $1.3 million from over 20 countries, approaching the $1.5 million in total consideration paid in the purchase.

As is typical in the cinema exhibition industry, customer capital spending activity slows substantially during the November and December holiday season. This upgrade pause allows exhibitors to maximize their revenue opportunity while they also work internally to complete budgeting and planning for theater upgrade priorities for the year ahead. We look forward to customers releasing their budget plans in the new calendar year so we can work to secure some of their projects and build that outlook into our public outlook for investors. At this point, we have a favorable outlook for project activity leading up to the holiday film release season.

Finally, as we have discussed previously, MiT continues to evaluate the merits of potential business combinations or other strategic transactions that we believe could enhance our competitive position, growth potential, and financial results for our shareholders. Now, I'll turn the call over to our CFO, Bart Bedard, to review the financial highlights.

Bart Bedard: We published our financial statements in this morning's press release and expect to file a Form 10-Q later today. Now I'll briefly walk through our financial results. MiT's Q1 2027 revenue increased 9.2% to $6.09 million, compared with $5.58 million in Q1 of 2026. The increase was principally attributable to two customers who accelerated the timing of projects by one quarter into Q1 of 2027, putting our results well ahead of our prior outlook. This is a very clear example of how the timing of larger customer projects can have on our quarter results and comparisons to other periods.

Our Q1 2027 results also benefited from $429,000 of DCS loudspeaker sales, including a large shipment to a customer in Sri Lanka, compared to $400,000 in DCS revenue in Q4 of 2026, and no revenue in the year-ago period prior to the purchase of DCS. Our DCS order backlog is approximately $459,000 today, and we are pleased with the pace of reception and inquiry by customers for the DCS line one year following the acquisition. Gross margin percentage in Q1 of 2027 decreased to 24.1% compared to 30% in Q1 of 2026, reflecting lower sales of high-margin cinema accessories products and increased costs.

Higher global transportation and input costs, particularly in international markets, also contributed to margin pressure during the quarter, increasing the cost of delivering products and equipment to customers. Our Q1 2027 gross profit was $1.47 million compared with $1.67 million in the prior year period, with the decrease attributed to the lower gross margin. Q1 2027 operating expense declined to $1.3 million from $1.32 million in Q1 2026, as MiT continued to benefit from certain cost initiatives put in place the past several quarters. Q1 of 2027 net income was $181,000, or $0.02 per share, compared with net income of $509,000, or $0.05 per share, in Q1 of 2026.

The decrease was due to the lower gross profit, as well as $128,000 of income from the extinguishment of payables that was recorded in Q1 of 2026. Turning to our balance sheet, we had working capital of $4.24 million at the close of Q1 2027, compared to $4.04 million in Q1 of 2026. MiT has no long-term debt. We closed Q1 2026 with net cash of $5.69 million and approximately $0.55 per common share, compared to net cash of $3.19 million in Q4 of 2026. The sequential increase reflects the management of the timing of accounts payable payments, as well as $1 million in customer deposits collected against future work.

Turning to our revenue outlook, MiT currently anticipates revenue of approximately $5.4 million in our fiscal 2027 second quarter ending December 31, supported by the delivery of a turnkey upgrade of a 16-screen theater complex. In summary, achieving positive net income this quarter is an encouraging milestone that reflects our solid customer engagement and the progress we have made in aligning our expense structure with the business. Our priority remains to build on this foundation through disciplined execution, profitable growth, and the conversion of our customer pipeline into revenue-generating projects. With that overview, operator, we are ready to begin the Q&A session.

Operator: Thank you. We'll now be conducting a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. A confirmation tone will indicate your line is in the question queue. You may press star two to remove your question from the queue. For participants using speaker equipment, it may be necessary to pick up your handset before pressing the star keys. One moment, please, while we poll for questions. As a reminder, if you'd like to ask a question, please press star one. Thank you. There are no questions at this time. I would like to hand the floor back over to management for any closing remarks.

At this time, we are concluding today's conference. You may disconnect your lines, and we thank you again for your participation.
